title: Diffusion Models from First Principles: From Images to Video & Text
description:
Note: Mandatory to fill both RSVP and fill in the Google https://forms.gle/hgBmNo5NHNekVYvm7 no last minute exceptions will be possible without completing both these steps.

Build a Diffusion Model from Scratch on 6 GB VRAM \| Image → Video → Audio → Text → Omni

How does a model learn to create an image, generate a video, produce text, or work across multiple modalities—starting from nothing but noise?

In this hands-on workshop, we will build an intuitive understanding of **diffusion models from first principles**, starting with the mathematics and fundamental idea of adding noise and learning to reverse that process.

We will then trace the **evolution of diffusion architectures**, from the early diffusion models to modern approaches used across **image, video, text, audio/multimodal, and Omni-generation systems**.

We’ll explore concepts such as:

* Forward diffusion and the reverse denoising process
* Noise schedules, timesteps, and denoising objectives
* DDPM and DDIM
* U-Net–based diffusion architectures
* Latent Diffusion Models
* Diffusion Transformers (DiT)
* Flow Matching and modern diffusion/flow-based architectures
* How diffusion evolved from image generation into video and multimodal generation
* How modern Omni models combine multiple modalities within generative architectures

The workshop will conclude with a **live implementation of a diffusion model from scratch**—building the forward-noising process, neural network, training loop, and reverse-generation process ourselves.

The entire hands-on implementation will be designed to run on a **consumer GPU with just 6 GB of VRAM**, making it possible to understand diffusion without requiring expensive hardware.

**From noise → mathematics → architecture → a working generative model.**

title: Context Layers for AI: Knowledge Graphs & Intelligent APIs
description:
**Note - To sign up for this event, you must register and be approved here: https://luma.com/q1yzh1r3**

Your AI app is only as smart as the data it can reach. Bolt a model onto a pile of disconnected tables and you get confident answers with nothing underneath them - an agent that can't tell you how it knows what it knows, and an API that hands back rows instead of insight.

​Every team building with agents right now is solving the same problem: where does the data, its relationships and its meaning actually live, so an agent can recall what matters and an API can return answers rather than raw records?

​We're teaming up with the Hyderabad GraphQL community for an evening on exactly that - knowledge graphs as the memory and context layer for AI with SurrealDB, and GraphQL APIs that use intelligent resolvers to deliver insight, not just data. Real talks, live demos, and time with engineers building on agents, graphs and modern APIs across the city.
​
Refreshments and plenty of time for networking.

**Note - To sign up for this event, you must register and be approved here: https://luma.com/q1yzh1r3**

description:
🚨 **BREAKPOINT 2026**

**“Every industry has one. Find it. Study it. Defend it.”**
**What happens when an industry appears to be growing, while underlying changes begin to disrupt the way it operates?**
**Breakpoint 2026 is a two-round case study competition that challenges participants to investigate real-world industry problems, identify underlying causes, develop evidence-based perspectives, and defend their recommendations before a jury.**
**This is not a conventional quiz with a predefined answer, nor is it a hackathon focused solely on building a product. There may be multiple valid perspectives, what matters is the strength of your reasoning, evidence, and ability to defend your decisions.**

🎟️ **CONVERGENCE PASS REQUIRED**
A valid Convergence Pass is mandatory for participation in Breakpoint 2026.
👉 Get your Convergence Pass:
[https://aspireup.ai/organization/convergence-vnrvjiet/event/10011](https://aspireup.ai/organization/convergence-vnrvjiet/event/10011)

**WHAT WILL YOU BE CHALLENGED WITH?**
Consider a problem such as:
India's IT Paradox
India's IT industry continues to grow, yet entry-level opportunities are becoming increasingly competitive.
• Is AI replacing entry-level work?
• Is the industry changing what it expects from fresh graduates?
• Is automation only one part of the story?
• What does this mean for students entering the workforce?
• What should students and the industry do in response?
You will not be given the answer.
Your team will have to research the issue, identify relevant evidence, determine the underlying causes, understand the stakeholders involved, develop an independent perspective, and present a practical recommendation.
And that is only Round 1.

**ROUND 1 — RESEARCH & PITCH**
Teams will randomly receive an industry problem and will be given a limited research and preparation window.
You will need to:
🔍 Understand the problem
📊 Identify relevant data and evidence
🧠 Analyse the underlying causes
👥 Evaluate the stakeholders affected
💡 Develop an independent perspective
🚀 Propose a practical solution or future outlook
Teams will then present their analysis and recommendations before a jury.
Be prepared to answer questions, justify your assumptions, and defend the important claims behind your argument.
The strongest 5–7 teams will advance to Round 2.

**ROUND 2 — THE COMPLEX CASE**
The challenge becomes significantly more demanding.
Qualifying teams will receive a new and more complex case involving multiple dimensions of a real-world industry problem.
With only 45 minutes to research and prepare, teams will need to:
• Quickly understand the situation
• Identify the key issues
• Evaluate competing trade-offs
• Make informed decisions
• Develop a defensible recommendation
The final presentation will be followed by deeper questioning from the jury.
There will be no opportunity for extensive preparation or rehearsed responses. Your ability to think, adapt and defend your reasoning will be tested.
RAPID FIRE — THE FINAL TEST
Think the final presentation is the end?
Not quite.
Finalists will face a rapid-fire tie-breaker. Each team will receive an on-the-spot question and have 30 seconds to respond.
No discussion.
No preparation.
Just your reasoning.

**PRIZE POOL — ₹10,000**
🥇 1st Prize — ₹5,000
🥈 2nd Prize — ₹3,000
🥉 3rd Prize — ₹2,000

**TEAM DETAILS**
Team Size: 3–4 members
Maximum Teams: 40
Build a team with people who can research, analyse, construct arguments, present ideas, and challenge each other's thinking.

**WHO SHOULD PARTICIPATE?**
Breakpoint 2026 is designed for students interested in:
🧠 AI & Technology
📊 Business & Strategy
🔍 Research & Analysis
💡 Problem Solving
🚀 Startups & Innovation
🎤 Presentations & Public Speaking
📈 Industry Trends
⚔️ Case Interviews & Consulting-style Problem Solving
You do not need to be an expert in every industry.

title: Generative AI: From Fundamentals to AWS
organizer: AWS User Group India AI ML
description:
Generative AI is rapidly changing how we build applications, work with data, and develop software. But what exactly is Generative AI, how do Foundation Models and LLMs work, and how do these concepts translate into real-world solutions on AWS?
In this session, we’ll start with the **fundamentals of Generative AI** and progressively connect those concepts to practical AWS services through hands-on demonstrations.

### What we'll cover

**1\. Generative AI Fundamentals**

* AI vs. Generative AI
* What makes Generative AI different
* What GenAI can create — text, images, code, audio, and video

**2\. Foundation Models & LLMs**

* What Foundation Models are
* How they differ from traditional task-specific models
* Understanding Large Language Models (LLMs)
* How a single model can perform multiple tasks
* Real-world Generative AI applications

**3\. Working with Generative AI**

* Prompt Engineering
* Few-Shot Prompting
* Understanding and handling hallucinations
* Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
* AI Agents and tool/API integration

### Live Demos

**Amazon Bedrock**
Explore Foundation Models, generate content, and see how **RAG and Knowledge Bases** connect models with external and enterprise data.
**PartyRock**
Build a Generative AI application without writing code, understand what happens behind the application, and see how user inputs can generate personalised results.
**Amazon Q Developer**
See how Generative AI can become part of the software development workflow — from generating and explaining code to debugging, fixing, and refactoring it.

### Bringing It All Together

We’ll close by looking at where Generative AI fits within the AWS ecosystem, including:

* **Amazon Bedrock** — building applications with Foundation Models
* **PartyRock** — experimenting and building GenAI applications without coding
* **Amazon Q Developer** — AI-assisted software development
* **Knowledge Bases** — connecting GenAI applications to enterprise knowledge using RAG
* **Agents for Amazon Bedrock** — connecting AI models to tools, APIs, and business workflows

Whether you're **new to Generative AI or already experimenting with LLMs**, this session is designed to give you a clear understanding of the concepts while showing how they can be applied using AWS.
Come learn the fundamentals, see the technology in action, and understand how to move **from Generative AI concepts to practical AWS solutions.**

**Want to upgrade your Python skills for the Quantum Era?**

You don't need a PhD in theoretical physics to program a quantum computer—you just need the right open-source tools. With Qiskit, software engineers and data scientists are already building and simulating quantum algorithms using Python.

The Mumbai Quantum Computing Group invites you to our live online session: "***Introduction to Qiskit Programming***"
In 60 high-impact minutes, we’re bridging the gap between classical coding and quantum execution, showing you how to construct, simulate, and run quantum programs.

**📅 Save the Date:**
🗓️ Date: Saturday, 26 September 2026
⏰ Time: 2:00 PM – 3:00 PM IST
📍 Mode: Online (via Google Meet)

Meeting link will be shared with the registered participants on the day of the event.

**What you'll learn:**
✅ The Qiskit SDK architecture and setup
✅ Building quantum registers, qubits, and circuit workflows in Python
✅ Simulating circuits locally vs. executing on IBM Quantum hardware
✅ Interactive Live Q&A

Whether you're a developer, researcher, student, or deep-tech enthusiast looking to expand your skill set, this session will give you a clear, actionable foundation.

🎟️ Slots are limited to keep the Q&A interactive— *RVSP* now to grab your spot!
